# Purpose

This report documents the accompanying `student_performance_analysis.R`
script. It demonstrates a beginner-friendly R workflow: generate fictional
student records, calculate descriptive statistics, and visualize simulated
exam scores against study hours.

All data are synthetic. The analysis is an exercise in R documentation and
reproducibility, not a study of real students.

## Questions

1. What are the mean, median, minimum, maximum, and standard deviation of the
   simulated numerical variables?
2. What does a scatter plot show about study hours and simulated exam scores?

# Inputs

The script requires no external dataset. It uses `set.seed(42)` to
generate 50 fictional observations.

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `student_id` | Fictional identifier (`S001` to `S050`) |
| `study_hours` | Simulated weekly study time (1 to 10 hours) |
| `attendance_pct` | Simulated attendance (60% to 100%) |
| `exam_score` | Simulated exam score, rounded and bounded by 0 and 100 |

The score formula includes study hours, attendance, and random variation.
Consequently, any relationships in the generated data are built into the
simulation and must not be interpreted as real-world evidence.

# Method and Code Examples

## Run the R script

The following R chunk executes the original script. Keep the `.Rmd` and
`.R` files in the same project folder when knitting. The script also
creates an `outputs/` directory containing CSV files and a PNG plot.

```{r run-script, results='hide'}
source("student_performance_analysis.R", local = TRUE)
```

## Preview the generated data

The first five fictional records provide a quick check of the dataset's
structure.

```{r preview-data}
head(students, 5)
```

## Summary statistics

The script calculates the mean, median, minimum, maximum, and sample standard
deviation of study hours, attendance, and exam scores.

```{r summary-statistics}
knitr::kable(
  summary_stats,
  caption = "Descriptive statistics for the synthetic student dataset"
)
```

## Scatter plot

The points represent individual fictional students. The red line shows the
fitted linear relationship between weekly study hours and exam scores.

```{r study-hours-plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5, fig.cap="Study hours versus simulated exam scores"}
plot(
  students$study_hours, students$exam_score,
  main = "Study Hours vs Exam Score (Synthetic Data)",
  xlab = "Weekly Study Hours",
  ylab = "Exam Score (%)",
  pch = 19,
  col = "steelblue",
  ylim = c(0, 100)
)
abline(
  lm(exam_score ~ study_hours, data = students),
  col = "firebrick",
  lwd = 2
)
grid()
```

# Outputs

Running the R script produces:

| Output file | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `outputs/student_data.csv` | 50 fictional student records |
| `outputs/summary_statistics.csv` | Descriptive statistics for the three numerical variables |
| `outputs/study_hours_vs_exam_score.png` | Standalone scatter plot with fitted trend line |

Knitting this document to HTML also produces an
`student_performance_analysis.html` report with the summary table and plot
embedded in the document.

# Interpretation and Limitations

In this simulated sample, the correlation between study hours and exam scores
is `r round(cor(students$study_hours, students$exam_score), 2)`.
This value is calculated when the document is knitted; it is not manually
entered.

Because the exam-score formula explicitly includes study hours and
attendance, the apparent association is part of the data-generation
process. Random variation and the 0-to-100 score limits also affect the
appearance of the plot. No conclusions about actual student performance
should be drawn from these results.

# Conclusion

The report demonstrates how to combine an existing R script with explanatory
text, reproducible calculations, a formatted statistics table, and a
visualization using R Markdown.
